![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

When mapping over `candidates`, there is no defensive guard to ensure that each `candidate` element is a valid object. If any element is nullish or malformed, accessing `candidate.candidate_id` will throw a `TypeError`. Filtering the array using `isObject` beforehand ensures the mapping is robust.

```javascript
  const candidates = Array.isArray(inputs.pilot?.candidates) ? inputs.pilot.candidates : [];
  const candidateAudit = candidates
    .filter((candidate) => isObject(candidate))
    .map((candidate) => auditCandidate(candidate, inputs.pilot))
    .sort((left, right) => compareByteOrder(left.candidate_id, right.candidate_id));
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When filtering or mapping arrays of objects, use defensive guards (such as checking if the element is a valid object) to ignore nullish or malformed elements instead of throwing a TypeError.
</details>

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The dereferencing of `inputs.pilotValidator?.checks` defaults to `[]` using the nullish coalescing operator (`??`). However, if `checks` is present but is not an array (e.g., a malformed non-array object), calling `.filter` on it will throw a `TypeError`. Using `Array.isArray` safely defaults to an empty array if the property is not an array.

```suggestion
  const failedPilotChecks = (Array.isArray(inputs.pilotValidator?.checks) ? inputs.pilotValidator.checks : [])
    .filter((check) => check && check.status !== 'pass')
    .map((check) => check.id)
    .sort(compareByteOrder);
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When dereferencing and mapping properties from potentially missing or malformed input artifacts, use Array.isArray to safely default to an empty array if the property is not an array, preventing TypeErrors.
</details>
